brief.goal: Rebuild this page as the site's listing: which puppies are available today, who their parents are, and the three steps from a first message to collection day — so a reader can go from 'which one' to 'reserved' without leaving the page, and so the machine-readable version of 'this dog, this price, still available' lives here and nowhere else.
brief.scope: Ten sections: hero, the three-figure counter strip, the six-puppy grid, the parents, the three buying steps, collection and delivery, one review, a five-row FAQ, the enquiry form and the close. All seven migrated images at their original paths; data/facts/buy-blue-staffy-puppies-uk.json records no embed for this page and none is placed.
brief.done: The page renders all six rows of data/puppies.json as cards, each with a Product node, an Offer and availability InStock, and it is the only page on the site that does; the counter strip reads its three figures from data; the three steps state the £500 refundable deposit and the 24-48 business hour reply and no other money figure; the delivery section links the price page's table rather than printing a second one; one review renders (Rachel L.) and the other two slots are not opened; five FAQ rows, one of them new and sourced here; all seven migrated images at their original paths; and no restatement of the £850 to £1,200 band, the £300 non-refundable deposit, the five weeks' free insurance, the 500-reader newsletter, the litter's counts and ages, the former city, or the four location towns — and it passes facts-preserved and link parity with nothing missing that `dropped` does not explain.

strategy.name: the listing
strategy.why: Four scanned pages list Staffordshire Bull Terrier puppies and not one marks a single dog up as a Product with an Offer — the closest of them puts eleven named puppies at £1,000 each on the page with no Product node anywhere, and the two classifieds mark up the page rather than the advert. Naming six dogs, pricing each one, saying who their parents are and marking each up properly is the gap, and it is what a listing page is for.
strategy.trade_off: A page built round six cards is a page that has to be rebuilt when the litter changes; every figure on it is therefore read from data/puppies.json and data/settings.json rather than typed, which is why no count and no age appears in the prose.
